title: US track and field nationals: Olympic stars and hopefuls deliver at LA 2028 ‘dress rehearsal’ | Athletics | The Guardian
description: The meet had lower stakes with no Olympics or worlds this year, but Nikki Hiltz, Sha’Carri Richardson and Cooper Lutkenhaus all took advantage of the moment
Author: Callum Jones
Headline: The meet had lower stakes with no Olympics or worlds this year, but Nikki Hiltz, Sha’Carri Richardson and Cooper Lutkenhaus all took advantage of the moment
Content: Sha’Carri Richardson reacts as she crosses the finish line in the women’s 100m final during this weekend’s USA Track & Field outdoor championships in New York.Photograph: Al Bello/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSha’Carri Richardson reacts as she crosses the finish line in the women’s 100m final during this weekend’s USA Track & Field outdoor championships in New York.Photograph: Al Bello/Getty ImagesAthleticsUS track and field nationals: Olympic stars and hopefuls deliver at LA 2028 ‘dress rehearsal’The meet had lower stakes with no Olympics or worlds this year, but Nikki Hiltz, Sha’Carri Richardson and Cooper Lutkenhaus all took advantage of the momentCallum Jonesin New YorkMon 27 Jul 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 27 Jul 2026 05.02 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIn two years’ time, tens of thousands of fans will pack into the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum – with tens of millions watching around the world – as the world’s fastest and strongest athletes compete at the 2028 Olympics.But this vast audience ebbs and flows in the long years between Olympics. On the other side of the country, around 5,000 fans filed into New York’s Icahn Stadium this weekend for the USA Track & Field national outdoor championships.After five consecutive years with either an Olympics or world championships, 2026 is the first without a major international outdoor track and field competition – lowering the stakes of this meet, without global qualification on the line.“There was nothing to lose,” Gabbi Jennings said after finishing second, behind Lexy Halladay-Lowry, in the women’s steeplechase final on Saturday afternoon. “Bit of a dress rehearsal.”More than a few stars did not make rehearsal. Absent Olympic champions included hurdler and sprinter Rai Benjamin; 1500m gold medalist Cole Hocker; 100m hurdles gold medalist Masai Russell; and sprinter Gabby Thomas.“I know not everyone is doing it this year, for various reasons, but I value a national championship, and I want to compete at it,” said Grant Fisher, Olympic bronze medalist in both the 5,000m and 10,000m at Paris 2024. “And I think, you know, people deserve seeing good athletes and performances.”For the fans and athletes who showed up in New York, the meet amounted to an early window into who Team USA could send out on to the track, and into the field, at their first Summer Games on home soil in three decades.“Honestly, I never viewed this as an off year,” said Nikki Hiltz, who this month ended Faith Kipyegon’s five-year winning streak at the Prefontaine Classic in Eugene, Oregon, where they won the women’s mile.View image in fullscreenNikki Hiltz crosses the finish line in the women’s 1500m.Photograph: Aviana Goode/USATFHiltz won the women’s 1500m – their fourth straight national title – in 4min 6.92sec on Saturday, ahead of Addy Wiley and Emily Mackay, who stumbled over the line. On Sunday, Mackay won the women’s 5,000m, and Wiley came second in the 800m, behind Nia Akins.Big namesOlympic gold and silver medalist Sha’Carri Richardson stormed the women’s 100m final to win in 10.77 seconds. Her training partner, Olympic gold and bronze medalist Melissa Jefferson-Wooden, steamed through the 200m final in 21.69 seconds.“I’m in a really good spot,” said Jefferson-Wooden, telling reporters she had wanted to set a new personal best this weekend – but that she is “absolutely” confident more will come. “Today told me everything I need to know.”View image in fullscreenNoah Lyles dominated the men’s 100m, but pulled up short in the 200m final.Photograph: Aviana Goode/USATFNoah Lyles, Olympic gold and two-time bronze medalist, equalled his lifetime best of 9.79 seconds in the men’s 100m final, seeing off Olympian Ronnie Baker, two-time Olympic silver medalist Kenny Bednarek and former world champion Christian Coleman.But Lyles pulled up before finishing the 200m final. “Not how I wanted that,” said Garrett Kaalund, of the University of Southern California, who won in 20.04 seconds.After the race, Lyles blamed cramp in his hamstring, which he suggested was the result of his performance in the 100m. “I wanted to push myself, to make sure that I knew what it felt like to try and get up the next day,” he said. “If this happens at the Olympics, I need to be ready for it. This does show me what it takes to keep going, which, y’know, kinda puts a perspective onhow kinda great Bolt was.”View image in fullscreenChase Jackson led the women’s shotput at the USATF outdoor championships.Photograph: Aviana Goode/USATFIn the field, Chase Jackson – who won the 2022 and 2023 world titles and came second in 2025 – won her 11th national title, clinching the women’s shot put by more than a meter.Tara Davis-Woodhall, who won gold in Paris, initially prevailed in the women’s long jump, only for her final attempt to be ruled a foul after review. She ended up in third place, a day after also coming third in the 100m hurdles. Olympic silver medalist Anna Cockrell won the women’s 400m hurdles, her first national title.View image in fullscreenTara Davis-Woodall competed in both the long jump and the 100m hurdles at the USATF outdoor championships.Photograph: Aviana Goode/USATFOnes to watchHigh school phenomCooper Lutkenhaus, 17, blazed through the men’s 800m final in 1:43.48, winning by the biggest margin in a US men’s outdoor 800m final since 2014 – ahead of Wes Ferguson and Hobbs Kessler, who ran a season’s best. (Donavan Brazier, who staged a fairytale comeback in 2025 after years of injury woes, unexpectedly failed to qualify in the heats.)Cooper Lutkenhaus: US track phenom on family ties, LA 2028 and balancing stardom with high schoolRead more“When you run 1:42 at 16 years old, you’re expecting that … there’s going to be a lot of pressure,” said Lutkenhaus, still holding the finishing tape. “There’s people thinking you should run this, run that. I’m not really focused on that. I’m just focused on what I can do.”Two-time Olympian Woody Kincaid outkicked Fisher in the final stages of the men’s 10,000m, winning by a second. “When the race got slow, I was ready, ready for it to take off,” said Kincaid. “I’m sure there were some doubters saying, ‘He’s 33,’ but I didn’t feel that when I finished the race.”Olympic men’s 400m champion Quincy Hall did not make it through the heats, setting the stage for one of the biggest upsets of the meet. Justin Robinson, an unsponsored athlete, was first across the line in the final, narrowly ahead of Chris Bailey, who won gold in the 4x400m relay at Paris 2024.Last year was “pretty difficult”, said Robinson, who had worked at Costco and a landscaping company to make ends meet. “I’m waking up at 2 o’clock in the morning just to get to work and practice at 3 in the evening, and not getting home until sometimes 7, 8 at night.”With a gold medal around his neck, Robinson expressed hope that a national title would help him land a sponsor. Within minutes, however, his victory was scratched from the record over a lane violation.“I mean, I get rules are rules,” said Bailey, who took the 400m title following Robinson’s disqualification. “But I don’t agree with it.”“I’m proud of him,” Bailey added, of Robinson. “This is a guy who was beating me all throughout college, and y’know, to see him finally making that transition, into the shape he was in college, is truly an honor to watch.”The opening ceremony of the LA Olympics, scheduled for 14 July 2028, is less than two years away. “I think about that almost every single day,” laughed Wiley.“It comes up so quick,” said Hiltz, who said they were trying to take things day by day. “In the back of my mind, like, it is this big looming thing – not in a bad way, but in a really, really exciting [way]: this is my main character moment. I want to see if I can medal on home turf.”Explore more on these topicsAthleticsOlympic GamesUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino accuses critics of spreading hate at World Cup | Gianni Infantino | The Guardian
description: Gianni Infantino has hit back at critics of the World Cup, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives
Author: Sachin Nakrani
Headline: Gianni Infantino has hit back at critics of the World Cup, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives
Content: Gianni Infantino with Donald Trump at the World Cup final. ‘We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness,’ said the Fifa president.Photograph: DiaEsportivo/Action Plus/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino with Donald Trump at the World Cup final. ‘We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness,’ said the Fifa president.Photograph: DiaEsportivo/Action Plus/ShutterstockGianni InfantinoFifa president Gianni Infantino accuses critics of spreading hate at World CupInfantino claims critics of World Cup ‘missed it all’He again defends Balogun affair and treatment of IranSachin NakraniMon 27 Jul 2026 04.49 EDTLast modified on Mon 27 Jul 2026 18.29 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Fifa president,Gianni Infantino, has launched an extraordinary attack at critics of the World Cup, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives, while defending the tournament as a success that celebrated unity, safety and inclusion.In a 15-part message published on Monday on Instagram, Infantino claimed detractors had overlooked the joy and togetherness experienced by millions of people around the world who witnessed the tournament,won by Spainand staged in the US, Canada and Mexico.Fifa president Gianni Infantino called to appear before Congress over Trump tiesRead more“You were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all,” the 56-year-old Swiss said. “To those behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we atFifaare ​on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering ‌the best show in the ‌world. We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness.”Fifa was criticised about a number of issues ‌during the World Cup, including US visa restrictions affecting supporters and officials from several countries, and concerns for teams from conflict-hit regions. Infantino’s open letter followed scrutiny of Fifa’s suspension of an automatic one-match ban imposed on the USA striker Folarin Balogunafter the intervention of Donald Trump. Officiating decisions in Argentina’s last-16 win against Egypt also received criticism,most strongly from the Egypt manager, Hossam Hassan.In his social-media intervention, Infantino said: “Potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide. It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising.”The Somali referee Omar Artan wasbarred from entering the USdespite having a valid visa, while the Iran team and staff were subject todifficult travel restrictionsimposed on them by the US government as a consequence of the war between the two countries. Infantino said: “Iran ​entered the United States without ‌incident or conflict. The Iranian team received visas to enter because football is about peace. It’s not about politics. Countries facing serious health issues or other challenges were granted visas.”Infantino’s letter is likely to lead to ridicule of the man who on the eve of the previous World Cup in Qatardeclared: “Today I feel Qatari. Today I feel Arabic. Today I feel African. Today I feel gay. Today I feel disabled. Today I feel a migrant worker.” It has certainly led to further criticism, with the human rights organisation, FairSquare, claiming Infantino’s statement shows he has become “divorced” from his unpopularity.“Infantino’s score-settling rant further underscores his unfitness to govern world football,” Nicholas McGeehan, director and co-founder of FairSquare, told the Telegraph. “He is cosseted by yes‑men inside the organisation and divorced from the reality of his unpopularity outside of it.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionFairSquare issued a formal complaint against Infantino to the International Olympic Committee, accusing him of breaching its charter by failing to adhere to rules on political neutrality “through statements or other clear expressions of support for the US president”. Infantino has been a member of the IOC since 2020.The IOC announced on Friday that it would not investigate Infantino as FairSquare’s complaint fell outside its ethics commission’s jurisdiction.Explore more on these topicsGianni InfantinoFifaWorld Cup 2026World CupnewsShareReuse this content

title: John Stones set for Inter move after shining for England at World Cup | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: The England defender John Stones is poised to complete a free transfer to Inter after leaving Manchester City
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: The England defender John Stones is poised to complete a free transfer to Inter after leaving Manchester City
Content: John Stones started the World Cup quarter-final and semi-final for England.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreenJohn Stones started the World Cup quarter-final and semi-final for England.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PATransfer windowJohn Stones set for Inter move after shining for England at World CupDefender left Manchester City on free transfer‘I still feel I have so much to give to a club’Jamie JacksonMon 27 Jul 2026 17.02 EDTLast modified on Mon 27 Jul 2026 18.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleInter are closing in on signing John Stones as a free transfer after the 32-year-old defender leftManchester Cityin June.Inter and their rival Italian club Juventus were interested in Stones before the World Cup and theNerazzurriare now in pole position to recruit him following his impressive form in England’s run to the semi-finals.Manchester City hope Rodri will sign new deal as Real Madrid weigh up offerRead moreStones made 13 appearances for City last season before being injured in December. Yet after being out for two months and staying injury-free, he was selected only five more times by City’s then manager Pep Guardiola.At the World Cup, Stones started the opening game for Thomas Tuchel’s team against Croatia, was an unused substitute against Ghana and Panama, made substitute appearances in the knockout wins against the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Mexico, before starting the quarter-final victory against Norway and the 2-1 semi-final defeat against Argentina.Towards the end of last season Stones spoke of his continuing ambition to play at the top level. “I still feel I have so much to give a club and I feel in a good moment physically,” he said. “There is a lot for me still to fight for in my career and a new challenge will be exciting. I’m keeping an open mind. I can take what I have learned here and maybe pass it on.”While Inter are confident of signing Stones, the deal could yet collapse should a requisite Premier League club express an interest.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionArsenal’s William Saliba is out for an extended period with a back injury, meaning a defender is needed for cover in Mikel Arteta’s squad. Chelsea under Xabi Alonso are expected to play with three centre-backs so are in the market to sign at least one. title: Chelsea explore surprise moves for Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: Chelsea are understood to be in talks over move to sign Danny Welbeck from Brighton and Jordan Henderson from Brentford
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Chelsea are understood to be in talks over move to sign Danny Welbeck from Brighton and Jordan Henderson from Brentford
Content: Chelsea targets Jordan Henderson (left) and Danny Welbeck.Photograph: Guardian Picture DeskView image in fullscreenChelsea targets Jordan Henderson (left) and Danny Welbeck.Photograph: Guardian Picture DeskTransfer windowChelsea explore surprise moves for Danny Welbeck and Jordan HendersonBrighton striker scored 13 goals in league last seasonVeteran Brentford midfielder has a year left on contractPA MediaMon 27 Jul 2026 16.58 EDTFirst published on Mon 27 Jul 2026 12.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea are understood to be in talks over a move to signDanny Welbeckfrom Brighton. The 35-year-old is a surprise candidate to bolster Xabi Alonso’s forward line after scoring 13 goals in 37 Premier League matches last season.In a further unexpected move, there are also reports the club are in negotiations to bring in England midfielder Jordan Henderson fromBrentford. The 36-year-old has a year left on his contract, but it is claimed the Bees would be willing to let him leave on a free transfer.John Stones set for Inter move after shining for England at World CupRead moreThe former Liverpool captain made 34 appearances for Brentford last season and was a member of England’s World Cup squad. He broke his arm when he fell over advertising hoardings celebrating their win over Mexico.Welbeck also has a year remaining on his deal and there is optimism a deal can be concluded as Brighton are understood to be willing to let the striker move for the right price.Should a deal be reached it would increase the likelihood of departures from Stamford Bridge, with uncertainty surrounding the futures of Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson. Delap is considered second-choice striker behind João Pedro, who impressed in his debutChelseacampaign with 15 league goals, while Jackson spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich and has attracted interest from Aston Villa.Delap had been expected to be given a second year to prove himself after an unsuccessful debut campaign following his £30m move from Ipswich a year ago, though this latest development would seem to cast doubt on his future.Interest in Welbeck and Henderson reflects a revised Chelsea transfer policy as the club seek to recruit more established players under Alonso.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWelbeck, who scored twice when Brightonwon 3-1 at Stamford Bridge last season, signed a 12-month deal in March which runs until the end of the 2026-27 season. If the move happens, Welbeck would join a long line of players and staff to make the switch from Brighton to Chelsea in recent years, including the goalkeeper Robert Sánchez, midfielder Moises Caicedo and striker João Pedro.Explore more on these topicsTransfer windowDanny WelbeckChelseaBrighton & Hove AlbionBrentfordnewsShareReuse this content

title: Trial to be introduced in bid to prevent goalkeeper tactical time-outs | Soccer | The Guardian
description: New measures will require managers to nominate an outfield player to leave the pitch if the game is stopped for a goalkeeper injury
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: New measures will require managers to nominate an outfield player to leave the pitch if the game is stopped for a goalkeeper injury
Content: In November the Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma was accused, by the Leeds head coach Daniel Farke, of faking an injury.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenIn November the Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma was accused, by the Leeds head coach Daniel Farke, of faking an injury.Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/ReutersSoccerTrial to be introduced in bid to prevent goalkeeper tactical time-outsMeasures planned to run throughout 2026-27 seasonIfab yet to give permission for proposed rule changePA MediaMon 27 Jul 2026 15.07 EDTLast modified on Mon 27 Jul 2026 15.36 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEnglish football will introduce a trial this season in an effort to end the goalkeeper tactical time-out.The trial – backed collectively by Pro Ref, the Football Association, Premier League, English Football League, Women’s Super League and the National League – aims to prevent goalkeeper injuries used to disrupt momentum and allow opportunities for tactical instruction.‘Born out of quality’: Webb vows to increase match officials from minority groupsRead moreThe new measures are pending permission from the game’s law makers, the International Football Association Board, but are planned to run throughout the course of the 2026-27 domestic season.“As part of the trial, if the game is stopped for a goalkeeper injury, the manager/head coach will be required to nominate an outfield player to leave the pitch immediately,” the governing bodies said in a joint statement. “The nominated player is required to remain off the field for a minimum of one minute after the restart of play.“The aim is to ensure genuine injuries continue to receive appropriate medical attention, while removing any potential sporting advantage associated with stoppages.”The trial will operate with several exceptions, including when a free-kick is awarded for a foul on the goalkeeper and they immediately require treatment – also, when the goalkeeper and an outfield player have collided and need attention, or the goalkeeper is bleeding.Last season the goalkeepereight-second rule was introduced, punishing a goalkeeper for holding the ball for that length of time with the award of a corner to the opposition. That rule change was deemed a success and, working alongside that this season, a five-second countdown will be used by match officials where players have delayed the taking of a throw-in or goal-kick.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionPlayers will also be given 10 seconds to leave the pitch when substituted, and this will come into operation from the start of the Carabao Cup on 1 August.Explore more on these topicsFootballRefereesLaws of footballnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Born out of quality’: Webb vows to increase match officials from minority groups | Referees | The Guardian
description: Howard Webb, Pro Ref chief’s refereeing officer, said a more diverse talent pool will likely lead to higher levels of quality and raise standards
Author: Morgan Ofori
Headline: Howard Webb, Pro Ref chief’s refereeing officer, said a more diverse talent pool will likely lead to higher levels of quality and raise standards
Content: Sam Allison (left) is one of only three Black referees to have officiated a Premier League fixture.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAView image in fullscreenSam Allison (left) is one of only three Black referees to have officiated a Premier League fixture.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAReferees‘Born out of quality’: Webb vows to increase match officials from minority groupsReferees’ body stands by diversity initiativesWebb believes diverse talent pool will ‘raise standards’Morgan OforiMon 27 Jul 2026 13.07 EDTLast modified on Mon 27 Jul 2026 16.15 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHoward Webb, England’s chief refereeing officer, has vowed to continue increasing the talent pool from under-represented communities in English football’s officiating pathway, rejecting the wider backlash against diversity initiatives.Addressing that historic under-representation has prompted a new direction. In June, the newly named Professional Referees’ Body (Pro Ref), formerly called Professional Game Match Officials, announced that Select Group 1, 2 and its supplementary list had been merged into a new, single Professional Referee Group in the men’s professional game and will largely service the Premier League and the Championship from the start of the 2026-27 season. Pro Ref said it would create flexibility in appointments and help to recognise a wider variety of talented match officials as part of the organisation’s new direction.At a conference held at the Emirates Stadium by Bamref – an advocacy group that helps to give voice to Black, Asian and mixed-heritage officials – Webb told the Guardian that Pro Ref’s diversity drive fosters healthy and important competition. “We’re doing it to increase the quality of the officials working at the higher end of the game,” he said, insisting the decisions behind it are “born out of quality, rather than any other aspect”.View image in fullscreenHoward Webb, the chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref.Photograph: Fabio de Paola/The GuardianIn March, Reform UK’s Suella Bravermanwrote to the Football Associationdemanding that it scrap its target for a quarter of England men’s coaching staff to come from minority ethnic backgrounds by 2028, calling the approach “utter woke nonsense”. The FA responded by defending the target as part of its wider commitment to reflecting the diversity of the game. Similar pressure has surfaced in US sport, where the NFL’s Rooney Rule isnow facing a legal challengefrom Florida’s attorney general. In the UK, employers can encourage applications and provide targeted training for under-represented groups.Webb argued that the visibility of refereeing makes tokenism impossible. “If you are not good enough to officiate in the Premier League you will be found out really quickly. There’s no real hiding places,” he said. A more diverse talent pool, he said, is “much more likely to bring higher levels of quality, greater choice, greater competition, and ultimately raising standards for all”.Farai Hallam is the latest example, following Uriah Rennie and Sam Allison as the third Black referee to officiate in the Premier League. In a defining moment, he waved away a penalty claim for Manchester City against Wolves in January,rejecting the video assistant referee’s advice.Danielle Every, the Pro Ref chief operating officer, said the organisation has seen a shift in attitudes since it introduced structural changes. “I genuinely feel that there is more acceptance and understanding of why these interventions are important,” she said, pointing to data showing zero Black representation among Premier League officials in 2022.View image in fullscreenFarai Hallam rejects Manchester City’s claims for a penalty despite a VAR review during January’s Premier League match at the Etihad Stadium.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAThe stance comes as Pro Ref overhauls how it identifies talent. Webb described moving away from solely relying on the traditional observer system – in which officials were marked out of 10 after every match and ranked on a performance table – towards a coaching-led model built around a new “matchday performance developer” role. That model will be rolled out in League One and League Two as well as the women’s professional game. In the Premier League and Championship, the key match incidents panel, a primary layer of accountability, will remain. Referees at all levels expect their matches and performances to be subject to review by individual coaches.The old system, Webb said, was “very rigid and restrictive”, and led to “some really good officials being left behind”. The change, he insisted, will help to surface talent from under-represented groups earlier than before.Aji Ajibola, who co-founded Bamref in 2019, welcomed the progress on numbers but warned it counts for little without sustained backing once officials are inside the system. “We now have a duty of care to those that we’re bringing into officiating, to make them feel safe,” he said, describing plans for wraparound support covering mental health and wellbeing alongside coaching and mentoring.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We’ve got expertise in our community, which then creates opportunities for us to get into other areas of the game,” he said, framing retention, not recruitment, as the next front in the campaign.Tension between visible progress and lived experience was echoed by Akil Howson, inducted into the Bamref Hall of Fame at this year’s conference after becoming the first Black official in an FA Cup final. “Broken down the barrier finally after 158 years and now hopefully that door will never be shut again,” he said of the milestone.Howson, who is entering his fourth season as a Premier League official, was blunt about how far the game still has to go. “I still go to some of my meetings and I’m the only Black person,” he said. “It’s getting better, but it’s frustrating because it’s not where it could really be.”On his induction into the hall of fame, Howson pointed to what it signals for those coming through behind him. “It just goes to show how important visibility and representation is.”Explore more on these topicsRefereesnewsShareReuse this content

title: Maldini and Leonardo resign from Italian FA after Pirlo appointment falls through | Italy | The Guardian
description: Paolo Maldini and Leonardo have reportedly resigned from their roles with the Italian football federation after Andrea Pirlo’s appointment as Italy head coach fell through
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Paolo Maldini and Leonardo have reportedly resigned from their roles with the Italian football federation after Andrea Pirlo’s appointment as Italy head coach fell through
Content: Andrea Pirlo is no longer in the frame for the head coach role due to his commercial ties to a Russian betting company.Photograph: Vanessa Carvalho/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenAndrea Pirlo is no longer in the frame for the head coach role due to his commercial ties to a Russian betting company.Photograph: Vanessa Carvalho/ShutterstockItalyMaldini and Leonardo resign from Italian FA after Pirlo appointment falls throughPirlo no longer in running for coach role over betting tiesPaolo Maldini only appointed technical director on 11 JulyAssociated PressMon 27 Jul 2026 17.26 EDTFirst published on Mon 27 Jul 2026 05.56 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GooglePaolo Maldini and Leonardo have reportedly resigned from their roles with the Italian football federation in the wake of Andrea Pirlo’s appointment asItalyhead coach falling through.Both figures had recently taken on roles as part of an overhaul of the national team management. Maldini ‌was appointed ‌on 11 ‌July as technical director of the Italian federation, to help to rebuild the national sideafter they failed to qualifyfor a third successive World Cup finals. But he has stepped down just 16 ‌days later alongside Leonardo, the former Brazil international who had been brought in as his adviser.Their exits come shortly after Pirlo said he was no longer in the running to coach the Italy side. His prospective appointment was the subject of fierce opposition over his commercial ties to a Russian betting company, Fonbet. The former Italy midfielder wrote on Instagram on Monday that he had “heard last night that I’m no longer the candidate for the Italy national team job”.The double departure creates ​an immediate crisis for the newly appointed federation president, Giovanni Malagò. It leaves the federation without a clear national team strategy at its lowest ebb in nearly 40 years, following early ⁠European exits for Italian clubs last season and another failure ​to qualify for ​the World Cup.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionPirlo had ​been Maldini’s primary choice for the job after Pep ​Guardiola rejected the ‌federation’s initial ​approach. Several other ​high-profile managers are now being linked with the vacancy, including Roberto Mancini, Thiago Motta and Antonio Conte.Explore more on these topicsItalynewsShareReuse this content

title: Spurs’ plans for new training facility in London park blocked by high court | Tottenham Hotspur | The Guardian
description: Judge quashes Enfield council’s decision to grant planning permission for new women’s and girls’ football academy
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Judge quashes Enfield council’s decision to grant planning permission for new women’s and girls’ football academy
Content: Eveliina Summanen (centre) celebrates with teammates after scoring for Tottenham Hotspur in their Women's FA Cup quarter-final against Chelsea in April.Photograph: Alex Davidson/The FA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenEveliina Summanen (centre) celebrates with teammates after scoring for Tottenham Hotspur in their Women's FA Cup quarter-final against Chelsea in April.Photograph: Alex Davidson/The FA/Getty ImagesTottenham HotspurSpurs’ plans for new training facility in London park blocked by high courtJudge quashes Enfield council’s decision to grant planning permission for new women’s and girls’ football academyPA MediaMon 27 Jul 2026 13.13 EDTLast modified on Mon 27 Jul 2026 13.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleA council’s decision to allowTottenham HotspurFootball Club to build a new training facility in a park in north London has been quashed by a judge at the high court.The campaign group Guardians of Whitewebbs told a hearing in June that Enfield council’s decision togrant planning permissionfor a new women’s and girls’ football academy on 6.5 hectares (16 acres) of land in Whitewebbs Park was unlawful.The group’s lawyers told the hearing in London that the council breached the rules when making its decision, as councillors were not provided with all relevant information regarding the development’s environmental impact, meaning they were “materially misled”.Campaigners also claimed there was a “real possibility of bias” in the decision as Spurs had “unparalleled access” to senior council figures at the time of the application.Enfield council, which was Labour-controlled at the time but is now run by a Conservative minority administration, withdrew its defence to the claim last month.But Spurs continued to oppose the challenge, claiming it should be dismissed as the result “would inevitably have been the same” had the information been provided.The club also said the allegations of bias were “completely overblown”.In a ruling on Monday, Sir Tim Kerr, sitting as a high court judge, quashed the decision to approve the plans, finding the result “could well have been different” had all the relevant information about the scheme been available.He dismissed claims concerning potential bias, describing the group’s arguments as “weak” and stating that “cordial relations” between the council and the club were “normal given the overlapping functions and interests”.Spurs agreed a 25-year lease for the site in 2023 – a decision that wasunsuccessfully challengedat the high court in 2024 – and the council resolved toapprove the planning applicationin February last year.The plans would have seen the construction of 10 football pitches and other work on the park, which is near the club’s men’s training facilities.Jenny Wigley KC, representing Guardians of Whitewebbs, said in written submissions that the ecologist Giles Sutton had carried out a report into the environmental benefits of the plans in November 2024.Sutton told the council that while he did not oppose the scheme “as such”, it was “counterintuitive” to accept the club’s claims that the site would benefit the local environment as about 40% of the park would be lost.“In my opinion, if the council were to accept this, their decision could be easily challenged,” he added.But Wigley said council officers had said in a planning report for councillors that there was “no objection to the proposed development”, despite Sutton telling the authority that this did not reflect his advice.She continued that Sutton’s report “clearly informed the planning officers’ views” on the environmental impact of the scheme and should have been presented as a “background document”, meaning members of the public could have inspected it.Wigley said: “[The law] does not permit this kind of salami slicing, where a planning officer can disclose parts of a report they agree with but can avoid public scrutiny of the parts of the report they do not agree with.”James Maurici KC, representing Spurs, said Sutton’s views were “no more than an assertion” and that Guardians of Whitewebbs had “failed to provide any evidence” that it had been prejudiced by the council’s failure to provide the document.He continued: “It is highly likely, indeed inevitable, given the absence of any evidence of prejudice, that the outcome for the claimant would not have been substantially different if the conduct complained of had not occurred.”But Kerr said the council’s noncompliance with rules was “serious” and that councillors were “materially misled” by the exclusion of Sutton’s report.Alessandro Georgiou, the Conservative leader of Enfield council since May 2026, said the authority was delighted with the decision and that it withdrew its defence as it would “not have been in the best interests of residents across the borough”.He added: “We said we would protect Whitewebbs Park from this unacceptable proposal and we will now move forward with plans that reflect the needs of the local community and also preserve and protect this important area of Enfield.”Explore more on these topicsTottenham HotspurTottenham Hotspur WomenPlanning policyLocal governmentWomen's footballnewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester City hope Rodri will sign new deal as Real Madrid weigh up offer | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Real Madrid are interested in Rodri after his World Cup performance, with the midfielder’s City contract expiring in June 2027
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: Real Madrid are interested in Rodri after his World Cup performance, with the midfielder’s City contract expiring in June 2027
Content: Gianni Infantino (left) and Donald Trump hand the World Cup to Rodri after the final.Photograph: Hannah McKay/ReutersView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino (left) and Donald Trump hand the World Cup to Rodri after the final.Photograph: Hannah McKay/ReutersManchester CityManchester City hope Rodri will sign new deal as Real Madrid weigh up offerReal Madrid interested after World Cup performanceMidfielder’s contract at City expires in June 2027Jamie JacksonMon 27 Jul 2026 09.44 EDTLast modified on Mon 27 Jul 2026 13.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleManchester City are hopeful that Rodri will sign a new contract, but the club are braced for a bid from Real Madrid for the midfielder as well as moves from other suitors.Rodri’s terms expire next June and he has failed to sign City’s new deal, which has been on the table for a while. The club are in talks with the 30-year-old and are optimistic these will prove successful.World Cup, Ballon d’Or, Champions League, Euros … has Rodri completed football? | The KnowledgeRead moreBut Real have now altered their previous stance of not being interested in Rodri after his hugely impressive displays as captain of Spain’s triumphant World Cup campaign – he won the Golden Ball as the tournament’s best player – and are understood to be preparing a bid.Rodri’s reliability during the summer has also allayed concern regarding his physical robustness after two injury-plagued seasons, although he is to undergo surgery on a back injury having returned to England from North America.In March, Rodri hinted at a desire to play for Real. “Having played for Atlético [in 2018-19] before would not prevent me from playing forReal Madrid,” he said. “There are other players who have done that before. Maybe not direct transfers, but eventually. You can’t turn down one of the world’s best clubs.”Real’s interest in signing Rodri may well initiate interest from other elite clubs. Barcelona could move for him after Frenkie de Jong’s medial collateral ligament injury ruled him out for months, while Paris Saint‑Germain are known to admire him.View image in fullscreenRodri won the Golden Ball at the World Cup for the tournament’s best player.Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/SportsphotoReal may need to generate finance in order to sign Rodri – especially if, as expected, theysign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig for a fee “well in excess” of €100m (£85m)– which may mean the sale of Aurélien Tchouaméni. The 26-year-old Frenchman is thought to have agreed a new contract with the club though this has not been announced. His current deal ends in summer 2028.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballPreview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionManchester United retain an interest in Tchouaméni but earlier in the window were unsure if the fee Real would demand for the midfielder – around £70m – was within their budget.Tchouaméni’s teammate Eduardo Camavinga is also on United’s radar and would cost €50m-€60m.Explore more on these topicsManchester CityReal MadridSpainTransfer windownewsShareReuse this content

title: Jon McConnell chasing Commonwealth Games treasure after rejecting Love Island | Commonwealth Games 2026 | The Guardian
description: Before these Commonwealth Games, Northern Irish boxer Jon McConnell made headlines for turning down the 13th season of Love Island
Author: Yara El-Shaboury
Headline: Before these Commonwealth Games, Northern Irish boxer Jon McConnell made headlines for turning down the 13th season of Love Island
Content: Jon McConnell is enjoying the limelight at the Commonwealth Games despite turning down Love Island.Photograph: François Nel/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJon McConnell is enjoying the limelight at the Commonwealth Games despite turning down Love Island.Photograph: François Nel/Getty ImagesCommonwealth Games 2026Jon McConnell chasing Commonwealth Games treasure after rejecting Love IslandNorthern Irish boxer one victory away from a medalTryagain Morning Ndevelo inspired by his nameYara El-Shabouryat SEC Centre, GlasgowMon 27 Jul 2026 18.15 EDTFirst published on Mon 27 Jul 2026 17.00 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBefore theseCommonwealth Games, Jon McConnell made headlines for turning down the 13th season of Love Island. Now the Northern Irishman is one win away from a medal after defeating India’s Sumit Sumit to reach the 70kg quarter-finals in Glasgow.“I didn’t expect [the attention] at all,” he said. “Someone sent me the interview [about Love Island auditions] and I was a wee bit shocked. I didn’t even know I said half of it. It was after a sparring session and with the adrenaline I was just saying different stuff.“Now I am just going along with it a bit; the lads were winding me up. But boxing comes first. Skills pay the bills.”English part-time sprinter bursts with ‘national pride’ and slams Games no-showsRead moreThe 23-year-old had to dig deep against Sumit to secure a 4-1 victory after finding himself down early before producing a strong finish. “I came from behind; from two rounds down basically,” said McConnell, who had a point deducted. “I am proud of myself.”Having arrived in Glasgow on Tuesday, McConnell said the days leading up to his opening contest had tested his patience. “It was a long wait to be honest with you. It was really long. It has been a week. Every day felt the same: it was wake up, training, rest. It was getting a bit monotonous. This here is what I live for.”Earlier, Namibia’s Tryagain Morning Ndevelo also booked his place in the quarter-finals. Named after the lesson his mother instilled in him growing up, he has carried that philosophy into the ring, producing a unanimous points victory over Bangladesh’s Md Ruhin Reza in the men’s 60kg competition.After receiving a walkover in the opening round when Trinidad and Tobago’s Anthony Joseph failed to make the call time, Ndevelo finally got the opportunity he had been craving to compete. On Sunday, Ndevelo had completed his ring walk through the smoke before discovering he was the only boxer inside the ropes. Joseph never answered the call to the ring, leaving the Namibian warming up alone before the opening bell sounded with just one fighter present.View image in fullscreenTryagain Morning Ndevelo is through to the quarter-finals of the men’s 60kg competition.Photograph: François Nel/Getty ImagesFor a boxer chasing a breakthrough at his third Commonwealth Games, it was hardly ideal preparation. “Today was nice,” he said after his fight against Reza. “I’m glad that I got to go into the ring. Got to face somebody. I can see my level.“A lot of hard work has gone into this. So at least I finally got a chance to practise what I have been learning. I was thinking: ‘Am I really fine?’ and ‘Am I ready?’ because I didn’t get a taste. At least now I know. I don’t feel tired. I have an extra level I can get to. I was excited to have him [Reza] at least show up.”Now, in Glasgow, he has the opportunity to take the next step, with his remarkable first name becoming one of the stories of these Games. “My mother is my whole world,” he said. “[Growing up], whenever I missed training or I was feeling down, I would be told: ‘You don’t have to miss training. Just show up. Even if you are not good, just show up.’ She has always been behind me and that itself is the definition of my name.“Every day you wake up in the morning and you have the chance to do what you didn’t do yesterday. That is why my middle name is Morning. Tuesday, Wednesday, whenever I fight again, I have the chance to better what I did here today. That’s all from her, for giving me this name. Every time I feel low, I get up and try again.”Explore more on these topicsCommonwealth Games 2026BoxingCommonwealth GamesnewsShareReuse this content
